items.title_orig: P.E.S.T. (con Jeff Ament) tornano con il quarto EP a giugno
items.article_text: Il progetto hardcore di Jeff Ament prosegue il suo viaggio tra Missoula, radici punk e nuove registrazioni con una formazione ormai stabile. A Missoula certe cose non spariscono davvero. Restano sotto pelle, cambiano forma, poi riemergono quando meno te lo aspetti. È una dinamica che attraversa da sempre il percorso di Jeff Ament e che nei P.E.S.T. trova una delle sue espressioni più dirette. La band hardcore punk guidata dal bassista dei Pearl Jam sotto lo pseudonimo di Jeff Diction pubblicherà un nuovo EP nel giugno 2026 via Drag Bunt Records, continuando un percorso iniziato nel 2021 e ormai diventato un progetto parallelo sempre più definito e coerente. La formazione è ormai consolidata: Dave Parsons alla voce, Charlie Beaton alla chitarra, Jeff Diction al basso e John Wicks alla batteria. Una struttura essenziale, pensata per andare dritta al punto senza sovrastrutture, con un approccio che resta fedele alla scena hardcore da cui tutto proviene. Anche questa volta l’artwork sarà firmato da Bobby “Draws Skulls” Brown, già autore delle copertine dei precedenti EP e figura ormai ricorrente nell’estetica del progetto. Un nome che i fan dei Pearl Jam conoscono anche per aver realizzato, insieme a Jeff Ament, il magnifico poster del concerto di Missoula del 2018. Dietro il nome Jeff Diction c’è una storia che precede tutto. Era lo pseudonimo usato da Ament nei primi anni Ottanta ai tempi dei Deranged Diction, la sua prima band hardcore punk nata in Montana molto prima di qualsiasi esperienza successiva. Una scena piccola, grezza, fatta di club locali, cassette e registrazioni che circolavano in modo quasi artigianale, ma fondamentale nella costruzione del suo linguaggio musicale. Non è un caso che nel 2009, oltre venticinque anni dopo la fine originale del gruppo, i Deranged Diction siano tornati insieme per pubblicare il nuovo album Life Support insieme alla riedizione del loro disco del 1983 No Art, No Cowboys, No Rules e suonare nuovamente dal vivo tra Seattle e Montana. Quello spirito non è mai sparito davvero. Ha semplicemente trovato nuove forme. Il nuovo EP segna anche il primo lavoro registrato dai P.E.S.T. con John Wicks alla batteria, musicista già da tempo vicino ad Ament con  i Deaf Charlie e coinvolto anche nella colonna sonora della serie FX Under The Banner Of Heaven, realizzata insieme a Josh Klinghoffer. Proprio i Deaf Charlie potrebbero tornare con un secondo disco tra il 2026 e il 2027, confermando un periodo particolarmente attivo sul fronte dei progetti paralleli. Come già accaduto nei due EP precedenti dei P.E.S.T., anche il nuovo lavoro conterrà una cover punk hardcore, diventata ormai una sorta di firma del progetto. Nel secondo EP la band aveva reinterpretato Face Forward dei Necros, storica hardcore band del Michigan, mentre nel terzo aveva chiuso il disco con Glue degli SS Decontrol, gruppo fondamentale della scena hardcore di Boston. Una scelta che conferma ancora una volta quanto il gruppo resti profondamente collegato alle radici dell’hardcore americano anni Ottanta che ha formato musicalmente Jeff Ament. In parallelo all’uscita del nuovo EP, i P.E.S.T. hanno già confermato tre concerti: il 20 giugno allo Zootown Festival di Missoula, il 27 giugno al Big Sandy Pig Roast e il 26 settembre alla decima edizione dell’Ohana Festival, che si terrà come sempre a Dana Point. Quest’ultima sarà anche la prima data della band fuori dal Montana. ﻿

items.title_orig: Pearl Jam anuncia primeiro show após saída do baterista Matt Cameron
items.article_text:
O Pearl Jam anunciou seu primeiro show desde a saída do baterista Matt Cameron. A apresentação está marcada para 27 de setembro em Dana Point, Califórnia, como a atração principal do terceiro e último dia do Festival Ohana 2026.

Idealizado por Eddie Vedder, vocalista do Pearl Jam, o evento chega à sua décima edição e terá o projeto solo de Vedder na programação. Outras atrações incluem Maná, Billy Idol , Bad Religion, Sugar, Alabama Shakes, Jon Batiste, Fontaines DC, Pixies e muitos outros.

Por enquanto, esta é a apresentação desde a saída de Matt Cameron e, até o momento, a banda não revelou quem será o baterista substituto. Há rumores da vinda do Pearl Jam ao Brasil para showno Rock in Rio 2026 e possíveis apresentações em outras regiões do Brasil, como em Minas Gerais.

Matt Cameron anunciou sua saída em 7 de julho, após 27 anos tocando com o grupo. Em entrevista, o baterista explicou que  “estava tendo alguns problemas com os shows de três horas e com as turnês constantes”. O músico também revelou que “quer fazer um set de 70 minutos de tirar o fôlego, e é nisso que estou me concentrando agora”.

Ele afirmou: “Estou em um ponto da minha vida em que quero redirecionar meu tempo e energia de uma forma que seja um pouco baseada no que quero seguir como artista neste momento. Também estou gravando músicas originais que venho escrevendo ao longo dos anos”.

"Mirror Ball is the 21st studio album by Canadian musician Neil Young, and features members of Pearl Jam. It was released on June 27, 1995 through Reprise Records. The album has been certified gold by the RIAA in the United States. Tying in with the album title, a mirror ball graces the album's cover art. Because of legal complications between their respective record companies, only Young's name appears on the album sleeve, although the members of Pearl Jam are credited individually in the album's liner notes." - Reprise Records

items.title_orig: Hugh Jackman and Kate Hudson called “monsters” by the son of ‘Song Sung Blue’ duo
items.article_text:
Michael Sardina Jr. said his father would be “rolling in his grave” over his portrayal

The real-life son of the character played by Hugh Jackman and Kate Hudson in the film Song Sung Blue called the actors “monsters” and criticised the film for what he calls “lies”.

The romantic drama stars Jackman and Hudson as Mike and Claire Sardina, who performed as the Neil Diamond tribute band Lightning & Thunder and became noted for being booked alongside popular acts such as Pearl Jam.

Although Mike passed away in 2006, Claire has given her full backing to the movie. However, in a new interview with the Daily Mail (via People), the couple’s son, Michael Sardina Jr., said his father would be “rolling in his grave” over his portrayal.

“Everybody thinks it’s such a wonderful film, it’s so touching. It’s all lies,” he said. “And it steals all the hard work that my father put in his entire life.”

He also alleges he was “purposely cut out of the film” despite claiming to be paid to be a consultant on the project alongside his sister Angelina (who is played by King Princess in the movie).

“Every interview that those monsters have been on national television don’t even mention my existence at all, even though I was the most prevalent force in my father’s life, even when I wasn’t in Wisconsin, because I’m his only son,” he said. “They didn’t even try to contact me . . . They didn’t try to get more information… They could have very easily asked [director] Craig [Brewer].”

Angelina would tell the outlet: “The only thing that was true is the love between my dad and Claire. It’s a beautiful story, but that’s not how it went down. And I guess that’s what’s upsetting because it’s a lie.”

Neither Jackman, Hudson, or the film’s producers have commented on the claims.
Song Sung Blue was released in cinemas on Christmas Day in the US, and New Year’s Day in the UK.

Last summer, Hugh Jackman was due to headline a huge London BST Hyde Park show, but had to cancel due to unforeseen circumstances.

items.title_orig: Bruno Mars Covers “Smells Like Teen Spirit” With Slash, Duff McKagan, & Chad Smith At Star-Studded Private Show
items.article_text:
2:15 PM EST on December 12, 2025

A private concert headlined by Slash and a rock supergroup Thursday night featured an impressive list of surprise-guest rock stars including Bruno Mars, Eddie Vedder, Anthony Kiedis, Brandi Carlile, and Yungblud.

The gig, the holiday party for Todd Boehly's holding company Eldridge Industries, was held at the Capitol Theatre in Port Chester, NY. The core band for the evening was the Dirty Bats — Slash plus his Guns N' Roses bandmate Duff McKagan on bass, Red Hot Chili Peppers drummer Chad Smith, and producer/aging rock star whisperer Andrew Watt. Leonardo DiCaprio was reportedly in the audience.

According to setlist.fm, the night featured a bunch of classic covers, as well as a few old favorites sung by the original artist. Things kicked off with Yungblud singing the Rolling Stones' "Start Me Up," Faces' "Stay With Me," and Black Sabbath's "War Pigs" (reprising his VMAs tribute to Ozzy Osbourne). Then Carlile came out to sing Led Zeppelin's "Black Dog," her own "The Story," and Queen's "Tie Your Mother Down." Then it was Kiedis' turn to perform Motörhead's "Ace Of Spades," Iggy And The Stooges' "Search And Destroy," Black Flag's "Nervous Breakdown," Sly & The Family Stone's "If You Want Me To Stay," and the Allman Brothers Band's "Whipping Post."

Vedder then took the stage to do three Pearl Jam songs — "Corduroy," "Better Man," and "Wishlist" — plus covers of the Rolling Stones' "Waiting On A Friend," Dead Boys' "Sonic Reducer," and Elvis Costello's "(What's So Funny 'Bout) Peace, Love And Understanding." The final big name to appear was Mars, who fronted the Dirty Bats for Led Zeppelin's "Whole Lotta Love," the Police's "Roxanne," the Jimi Hendrix Experience's "Fire," Michael Jackson's "Dirty Diana," and Nirvana's "Smells Like Teen Spirit." Mars had mashed up "Smells Like Teen Spirit" with Jackson's "Billie Jean" a few times over the years, but apparently never did a proper version until Thursday night.

The evening ended with full-group singalongs of Chuck Berry's "Johnny B. Goode" and Neil Young's "Rockin' In The Free World." Seems like it must have been pretty fun. Check out footage from the show below.

items.title_orig: Jim Carrey inducts Soundgarden as band reunite alongside Taylor Momsen, Jerry Cantrell & Mike McCready at Rock & Roll Hall of Fame Ceremony
items.article_text:
“When the Seattle music scene exploded, it resurrected rock and roll for me,” Carrey said in his induction speech

Soundgarden have been inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame. See all the highlights from the ceremony below.

Last night (November 8) saw the annual ceremony take place at Los Angeles’ Peacock Theater, with the inductees including The White Stripes, OutKast, Cyndi Lauper, Chubby Checker, Bad Company and Joe Cocker.

Soundgarden were welcomed with an all-star induction that included a performance by the band’s surviving members, a group composed of fellow Seattle musicians and the daughter of the late Chris Cornell, who helped found the iconic grunge band back in 1984, and was the frontman up until his death by suicide on May 18, 2017.

They were inducted by Jim Carrey, who once hosted a 1996 episode of Saturday Night Live where Soundgarden was the musical guest. “Spank you kindly, spank you all,” he told the crowd as he opened his speech.

“You might ask why would Soundgarden – the heaviest of rock and roll royalty – want Jim Carrey to induct them into the Hall of Fame? Is there some deep, cosmic connection between them, or was the ‘Spoonman’ not available?”

Carrey went on to reveal that when he hosted SNL, he insisted that Soundgarden be the musical guest, and was gifted Cornell’s Fender Telecaster after the show. “When the Seattle music scene exploded, it resurrected rock and roll for me,” he said. “When I heard Soundgarden for the first time, I wasn’t just excited. I wanted to put a flannel shirt on and run into the streets screaming, ‘My mother smoked during pregnancy!’”

Following Carrey’s speech, Cornell’s daughter, Lily, joined the stage. “I am just really, really happy that he got to make music with his friends,” she said of her father. “At the end of the day, that’s what it’s all about. I know how much purpose that gave him, and how much it’s meant to people who have heard that music. That’s what I’ll be holding in my heart tonight.”

Each member of the band: guitarist Kim Thayil, drummer Matt Cameron, bassists Ben Shepherd and Hiro Yamomoto, who left the group in 1989, also delivered induction speeches. “Chris Cornell, we are so missing you tonight on this stage,” Yamomoto said. “We’ve heard so many stories of how the music we created became your own, and that is the greatest recognition of all. To everyone else out there – especially all you brown kids – let’s rock!”

Afterwards, a performance indebted to the Seattle music scene commenced, with Pearl Jam’s Mike McCready, Alice in Chains’ Jerry Cantrell, Brandi Carlile and Taylor Momsen of the Pretty Reckless (who served as opening act on Soundgarden’s final tour prior to Cornell’s 2017 death), joining the band onstage for ‘Rusty Cage’ and ‘Black Hole Sun’. Watch a clip below.

After the all-star Seattle performance, Cornell’s daughter Toni and Heart’s Nancy Wilson teamed up for an acoustic rendition of ‘Fell on Black Days’.

In other news, the surviving members of Soundgarden have previously spoken about an unreleased album featuring late frontman Cornell.
